## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Jambukhādakajātaka* (Ja 294) is a birth story preserved in the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. The narrative opens with the verse incipit *Ko 'yam bindussaro vaggu* ("Who is it sits..." / "Wer ist dies, dessen volle Stimme lieblich...") [SuttaCentral; Mylius 2003; Fausböll 1879]. The frame story (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) in Rājagaha, delivered by the Buddha concerning Devadatta and Kokālika [SuttaCentral; Mylius 2003; Fausböll 1879]. In the framing account, as Devadatta's gain and honor dwindled, Kokālika visited prominent families praising Devadatta's virtues and royal lineage [Mylius 2003; Fausböll 1879]. In the story's identification (*samodhāna*), the jackal is identified with Devadatta, the crow with Kokālika, and the tree sprite (*rukkhadevatā*) with the Bodhisatta [Fausböll 1879]. Variants of the title recorded in the commentary's manuscript tradition include *Jambukhāda-jātaka*, *Jambu-vādaka-*, and *Jambusākhāda-* [Fausböll 1897]. Klaus Mylius notes that the fable motif—wherein a flatterer (here a jackal/fox) praises the bird to obtain the fruit (or cheese in later European variants like La Fontaine)—reappears in varied forms in world literature and the *Tantrākhyāyikā* [Mylius 2003].
No cross-language parallels with score ≥10 are recorded by DharmaNexus, nor are external parallels listed on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, DharmaNexus identifies 10 text-reuse segments shared directly between this Jātaka text and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus].
